az_polychrome_dome.blurb: Polychrome Dome is one of the domes up Lost Canyon on the east side of Cochise Stronghold. Its face looks south and is nicely featured. Eight routes, mostly trad with a couple of bolted lines, run from easy fifth class up to about 5.10, so it suits parties after moderate multi-pitch climbing. Bring a 70 m rope if you have one, though 60 m is workable. Getting here is the catch: the trail climbs steeply past several other domes and takes well over an hour, which keeps the place quiet.
az_polychrome_dome.approach: From the main trail, turn onto the Lost Canyon Trail and climb steadily past large boulders, then continue beyond Chalkboard, Surrealist and Cholla's domes to Polychrome. Allow more than an hour. A lower Lost Canyon loop trail also circles the dome.

az_esperero_spires.blurb: Esperero Spires are a cluster of weathered granite columns on the divide between Esperero and Bird canyons, in the Catalina foothills above Tucson. All eight routes here are trad, running from about 5.6 to 5.9, with most near the top of that range. Rock quality varies, so test your holds. The setting is remote: a roughly nine mile round trip with a lot of elevation gain, no water, and a final off-trail scramble up through boulders to the base. The formation sees shade in the morning and sun later in the day. Spring and fall suit the long walk best.

az_east_end_wall.blurb: East End Wall is the easternmost wall on the South Side of Volunteer Canyon, in the Sycamore Canyon area of northern Arizona. It is a steel-gray basalt face where most of the front columns have broken away, leaving a handful of thin, solid lines. All eight routes are trad, ranging from 5.10 up to a single 5.13, with the bulk at 5.10 or 5.12: a few hard test pieces and a couple of easier warm-ups. The wall faces northwest and stays in shade all day, which is a relief in summer even though the rim above can bake. Faint trails lead to the base, and routes are reached by rappelling in.

az_wild_wall.blurb: Wild Wall is a basalt cliff at Paradise Forks, in Sycamore Canyon west of Flagstaff. The rock is gritty and covered with colorful lichen, and each line offers positive face holds. All eight routes are trad, with most at 5.10 to 5.11 and one at 5.12. It sits away from the busier crags, so it stays quiet and rarely sees traffic. It continues the line of the Jungle Wall and can be spotted from the Sine and White walls across the canyon. Like the rest of the Forks, routes are typically reached from the rim.
az_wild_wall.approach: From the parking area, take the right-hand fork, cross the seasonal watercourse, then follow the established rim trail until you are across from the White Wall.

az_lifestyles_rock.blurb: Lifestyles Rock is a satellite boulder area of Groom Creek, on a pine-covered hillside south of Prescott along Senators Highway. A large boulder with problems on every side anchors the spot, with a few smaller stones nearby that also have good lines. Eight problems are on record here, spanning V2 to V11, with a cluster of hard problems in the V7 to V8 range and plenty of difficulty above and below. It is a short walk off the main Groom Creek boulderfield and a good add-on for stronger boulderers.
az_lifestyles_rock.approach: Cross the road from the main Groom Creek boulders and the Island, pick up the horse camp trail that runs roughly alongside the road, and follow it until a huge boulder appears among the trees.

az_npr_wall.blurb: NPR Wall is a limestone bouldering wall on the Drysdale Trail, part of the Ridge area near Lake Mary outside Flagstaff. Its eight problems run from V0 to about V6, spread fairly evenly, so it works for a mixed group. Expect vertical sections and some bulges, with good landings. The trail linking the walls is narrow and tends to overgrow, and grades here are loose community estimates, so treat them as rough guidance.

_expect.name: The Son Tower aka Sun Tower

az_n_the_son_tower_aka_sun_tower.blurb: The Son Tower, also spelled Sun Tower, is a partly detached tower on the right side of The Pit, a limestone sport area south of Flagstaff off Lake Mary Road. It holds eight bolted routes with a good supply of moderates: one near 5.7, a few at 5.9, a couple of 5.10s, and two harder lines at 5.11 and 5.12. The stone is fairly solid but broken by ledges. It stays shaded on hot days, which helps in warmer months. Find it by walking the main trail past the Oven until a bolted tower appears.
